title: In general or in particulars: why the details bring G-d close
overview: "This is the chapter about the *prat*." Should the *hisbonenus* go in general, that G-d fills everything and everything is *batel* to Him, or particular by particular? The general is the real goal. But on its own it lets a person say "all is one and one is all" and understand it *mamash* backwards: G-d stays far away, and the merely general meditator can end in false visions. The particular way goes bottom-up, from what we really grasp, even if that is only our own *tevuna*, "just psychology". From the cold day and the sweater, the gas bill and the price of oranges, one follows the trail like Columbo through the *galgalim*, the angels and the *sefiros* of each world to *Malchus* of *Atzilus*, the Name *Elokim*, and then through the *partzufim* to the *Kav*. Each unification is a *prat* of a higher one; the *yichud klali* is the *bittul* of all of it to the Essence. The particular needs the general, and the general the particular, like the engineer's airplane. Every detail is aimed at the Essence; a beginner davens in general first. And for us, with two *lechatchila aribers*, the book is *Shaar HaYichud*.

sections.title: The question: contemplate in general, or in particulars
sections.summary: Should the *hisbonenus* take G-dliness as one general idea (*derech klal*) or go through it world by world and level by level (*derech prat*)? Even the general way has many analogies and details, but they all serve one general idea, in *yichuda tata'a* and in *yichuda ila'a* alike.

phrases.he: (ד) ומעתה יש לבאר באיכות ענין ההתבוננות,
phrases.en: (4) Now we must explain the manner of the *hisbonenus* (contemplation):

phrases.he: אם דרך כלל או דרך פרט דווקא,
phrases.en: whether in a general way or *davka* in a particular way.

blocks.text: "This is the chapter about the *prat*": the chapter about the particular, and that is what is wanted here, that the material has to be learned in a particular manner. The question it opens with is the manner of the *hisbonenus* (contemplation): **whether in a general way or *davka* in a particular way**, *derech klal* (the general way) or *derech prat* (the particular way).

phrases.he: כמו על דרך דוגמא בהשגה אלקית דבחינת ממלא כל עלמין,
phrases.en: For example, in the G-dly comprehension of *memalei kol almin* ((the light) that fills all worlds):

phrases.he: דרך כלל בג' עולמות בי''ע,
phrases.en: in a general way, in the three worlds of *Beriya, Yetzira and Asiya*,

phrases.he: הכל שרש ענין א' הוא
phrases.en: it is all the root of one matter,

phrases.he: בכל המשלים דזיו והתפשטות או אותיות כו',
phrases.en: in all the analogies of a radiance and a spreading forth, or of letters;

phrases.he: וכללותו רק ענין הגלוי מן ההעלם
phrases.en: and the whole of it is only the revelation of what is hidden.

phrases.he: או כמו ערך הנבדל לבחינת בעל גבול מחודש
phrases.en: Or like the incomparable distance of a newly made limited thing

phrases.he: לגבי בלתי בעל גבול דרך כלל,
phrases.en: from what is without limit, in a general way:

phrases.he: שיש בזה ריבוי אופנים,
phrases.en: there are many ways in this,

phrases.he: והכל בכלל,
phrases.en: and it is all general,

phrases.he: גם שנמצא בזה ענינים פרטים הרבה (כמו שיתבאר)
phrases.en: even though there are many particular matters in it (as will be explained).

blocks.text: First the general way, in *memalei kol almin*: in the three worlds of *Beriya, Yetzira and Asiya* it is all one matter, whatever the analogy, a radiance spreading forth or letters: **the revelation of what is hidden**. Or else the general idea that the newly made, limited thing is totally incomparable to what is without limit. And **there are many ways in this**: "there's a lot of *meshalim* even in a *derech klal*."

In general the *Aibershter* fills the world like the soul fills the body, or like the sun, "or like whatever, you know, all the different *inyanim*." And He is totally incomparable, like a newly made limited thing, "and stuff like that". Basically everybody is aware of these *inyanim*; not exactly with all the *meshalim*, but in general they are aware of it.

So a *derech klal* does not mean just one way, with no *orech* (length), *rochav* (breadth) and *omek* (depth). Even though there are many ways, **it is all general**: the general thing of it. **Even though there are many particular matters in it**, even in the *derech klal* there are a lot of different particular *inyanim*, as he is going to explain later.

phrases.he: או דרך פרט,
phrases.en: Or in a particular way:

phrases.he: להתבונן בכל עולם ובכל נברא
phrases.en: to contemplate each world and each creature

phrases.he: ובכל פרטי מדריגות חלוקים בסדרי ההשתלשלות מעילה לעילה
phrases.en: and all the particulars of the distinct levels in the order of the chain of descent, from cause to cause,

phrases.he: בכל אחד בפני עצמו דוקא כו'
phrases.en: each one by itself, *davka*.

blocks.text: **Or in a particular way**: whether we have to do it in a particular way, contemplating **each world and each creature** and every level of the chain from cause to cause, **each one by itself**. Not just in general that the *Aibershter* fills up the world like a soul fills a body, but exactly. With a soul filling a body, too, there is the general thing that everybody knows, that a soul fills a body. But then there is: how does it work on the eye? How does it make your tooth grow? "Stuff like that": in a particular, particular way, each one by itself.

phrases.he: וכך הוא השאלה בהתבוננות ביחודא עילאה
phrases.en: And so is the question in contemplating *yichuda ila'a* (the higher unity):

phrases.he: באורות וכלים דאצילות
phrases.en: in the lights and vessels of *Atzilus*,

phrases.he: בכל פרטי עשר ספירות עד עצמות אור אין סוף
phrases.en: in all the particulars of the ten *sefiros*, up to the Essence of the *Or Ein Sof* (the infinite light):

phrases.he: אם להתבונן בכללות ענין אור האצילות באיכות צמצומו מן העצמות
phrases.en: whether to contemplate in general the light of *Atzilus*, how it is contracted from the Essence,

phrases.he: ואיך שנבדל הערך לגבי עצמות המאציל
phrases.en: and how it is incomparable to the Essence of the Emanator,

phrases.he: ואיך דאיהו וחיוהי חד כו'
phrases.en: and how "He and His life are one"

phrases.he: (גם שיש בו ענינים פרטיים הרבה מאד כמו שיתבאר)
phrases.en: (even though it has a great many particular matters, as will be explained),

phrases.he: בכמה מיני משלים כמו שלהבת הקשורה כו' שנזכר בספר יצירה
phrases.en: through various kinds of analogies, like the flame bound [to the coal], mentioned in *Sefer Yetzira*,

phrases.he: או כענין גלוי ההעלם דכחות הנפש מעצמות הנפש דרך כלל כידוע
phrases.en: or like the revelation of the hidden powers of the soul from the essence of the soul, in a general way, as is known.

blocks.text: The same question is asked of *yichuda ila'a*, the lights and vessels of *Atzilus* up to the *Atzmus* (Essence) of the *Ein Sof*. One can contemplate in general how the light of *Atzilus* is contracted from the *Atzmus* and is incomparable to the Emanator, and how **"He and His life are one"**: how in general the *sefiros* of *Atzilus* are really unified, and how the light from the infinite light is contracted in order to come into them. This too has a lot of *pratim* (particulars), as will be explained. And it is done **through various kinds of analogies**: the flame bound to the coal of *Sefer Yetzira*, or the powers of the soul revealed from the soul's essence, "in general".

phrases.he: עד שאחר העיון יושג בחינת העומק מזה
phrases.en: until after the *iyun* (close analysis) the depth of it is grasped,

phrases.he: כנזכר לעיל בהשגה דממלא כל עלמין שנקרא יחודא תתאה כידוע.
phrases.en: as said above of the comprehension of *memalei kol almin*, which is called *yichuda tata'a* (the lower unity), as is known.

blocks.text: The general way goes on **until** one understands the depth of it: that in terms of *memalei kol almin* the worlds of *Beriya, Yetzira and Asiya* are full of G-dliness, understood in a general fashion, or that the world of *Atzilus* is unified with the Emanator. So the *inyanim* of *yichuda ila'a* and *yichuda tata'a* can basically both be discussed in a general manner.

And what he is calling a general manner is actually a particular manner, compared to what most people consider this *hisbonenus* has to be. "Because most people, especially in our days, they don't even go this far." They just say, well, yeah, G-d fills everything, it's all one. As one of the students said: "the world is the universe, and the universe is the world", and they figure they *chap* it (have got it) already.

sections.title: The general way holds the goal
sections.summary: The two ways are not alike. The general way has the real advantage: it reaches the depth of the whole, the Essence of the G-dly light, which is the real goal; the details of how the letters come out of the mind are not what one is after.

phrases.he: והנה באמת לא ראי זה כו'
phrases.en: Now in truth, one is not like the other.

phrases.he: דיש מעלה בהתבוננות דרך כלל
phrases.en: For there is an advantage in contemplation in a general way:

phrases.he: כדי שיוכל לבא לבחינת העומק בכלל שהוא בחינת עצמות אור האלקי
phrases.en: that he can come to the depth of the general, which is the Essence of the G-dly light,

phrases.he: בבחינת הכלל,
phrases.en: as a general whole,

phrases.he: בין ביחודא עילאה בין ביחודא תתאה,
phrases.en: whether in *yichuda ila'a* or in *yichuda tata'a*;

phrases.he: שזהו עיקר התכלית בגלוי אלקות בנפש כו'
phrases.en: for this is the real goal, the revelation of G-dliness in the soul.

blocks.text: **In truth, one is not like the other**: the two ways are really not alike. On one side, there really is an advantage in the general thing, **that he can come to the depth of the general, which is the Essence of the G-dly light**. In other words, the real thing is really *davka* in the *derech klal*.

It is just like what was said in chapters 1 and 2, especially chapter 1: why are we going for the *bina* (understanding), since the real thing is the *chachma* (wisdom)? Here it is basically the same thing. *Chachma* is the *klal* (the general whole) and *bina* is the *prat* (the particular). Here too, what you are really going for is to understand the main thing, the *klal*.

**Whether in *yichuda ila'a* or in *yichuda tata'a***: you want to understand how G-d fills up the world, in *yichuda tata'a*, and how, in *yichuda ila'a*, the *sefiros* are unified with the Emanator. "That's what you really want." You do not need all the particulars, like what it has to do with anything that the letters come out from *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *tevuna*, and that they started in the *machshava iyunis* (analytical thought). That is not really what you want to find out about.

Especially when you really get into the nitty-gritty of *meshalim* like that, you are not even talking about G-dliness necessarily. You can get into a *mashal* where it seems you are not talking about G-dliness at all. You are talking about, "what do they call that, there's a word for that," how language is made up. A student: "Semantics." "No, no, there's another word for that. Not semantics. Semantics is the meanings in language. But there's another thing of how the..." "Etymology." "Etymology, yeah." It seems you are talking about how the letters come out of the mind, and how the mind cuts the thing up into letters: "that's not really what you want to get to."

So there is a special advantage really in a *derech klal*, which talks about the main thing: how G-d is everywhere in everything, and how everything is *batel* (nullified) to the *Aibershter*. **For this is the real goal, the revelation of G-dliness in the soul**, not the *derech prat*. "The *derech klal* is the real goal. The real goal that we're shooting for is the *derech klal*."

sections.title: The general alone fools a person; the particular brings G-dliness close
sections.summary: One who has only the general idea can believe he understands while G-d is far from him, and understand it the opposite of how it is. What is grasped in particulars is grasped *mamash*, even if at first it is only how things work in ourselves, and from each particular one climbs to the one above it, until the general is reached without fooling oneself.

phrases.he: ויש מעלה בהתבוננות דרך פרט דוקא
phrases.en: And there is an advantage in contemplation *davka* in a particular way,

phrases.he: מצד עוצם הקירוב גלוי אור האלקי בנפשו יותר,
phrases.en: because it brings the revelation of the G-dly light much closer to his soul.

phrases.he: כי בהתבוננות דרך כלל יוכל להטעות את עצמו
phrases.en: For in contemplation in a general way he can fool himself,

phrases.he: עד שנדמה לו כי מאד קרוב אליו הדבר
phrases.en: until he imagines that the thing is very close to him,

phrases.he: ובאמת מרחוק מאד יהו״ה נראה לו
phrases.en: and in truth G-d appears to him from very far away,

phrases.he: בהיותו דרך כלל לבד
phrases.en: since it is only in a general way.

blocks.text: **And there is an advantage in contemplation *davka* in a particular way**: it brings the revelation of the light to his soul much closer. Why? **For in contemplation in a general way he can fool himself**, till he imagines that he really is understanding something.

**And in truth G-d appears to him from very far away.** The one who says, "Oh, G-d is all and all is everything and all is one," really has only a very vague idea, like what one of the students said before: he can take that general thing and understand it in a way that is actually exactly the opposite from the way it really is. He thinks he understands it well, and really the way he understands it is *mamash* the opposite of what it is. Why? Because it is just a general thing, and he does not really know the actual particulars of how it is like that.

phrases.he: מה שאין כן ההתבוננות דרך פרט,
phrases.en: Not so contemplation in a particular way:

phrases.he: שכל פרטי בהשגה בדבר פרטי,
phrases.en: a particular intellect grasping a particular thing

phrases.he: הרי יוקבע בנפשו בבחינת הקירוב ביותר
phrases.en: is fixed in his soul in the greatest closeness.

phrases.he: וממנו יבוא להשגת דבר פרטי העליון הימנו
phrases.en: And from it he will come to grasp the particular thing above it,

phrases.he: בהדרגה,
phrases.en: step by step,

phrases.he: עד שיבוא לכלל ההשגה בכלליות,
phrases.en: until he comes to the general comprehension as a whole;

phrases.he: שאז מתאמת יותר בלתי הטעות את עצמו כלל
phrases.en: and then it is truer, without fooling himself at all.

blocks.text: **Not so contemplation in a particular way**: thinking about particular ideas, in their various explanations, in particular *inyanim*. These are **fixed in his soul in the greatest closeness**: they come into his soul, meaning that his will is connected with his mind in a very close way.

**And from it he will come to grasp the particular thing above it.** A particular such as *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *tevuna*, or how *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *Asiya* comes off into the *kelipos* (the husks), he can understand very, very well. Even at the level where he cannot have a grasp of the *mahus* (what the thing is in itself), he can have *mamash* an actual grasp of the *metzius* (existence): to know exactly how the *metzius* of these things is.

And from that he can understand the level higher than it. Even when we talk about *Atzilus*, what we are really talking about is *Malchus* of *tevuna*, not even of the *kelipos* in general but of our own particular *kelipa*. That is really what we understand. Before, when we talked about what is *chachma*, what is *bina*, what is *bina* of *chachma* and *chachma* of *bina*, and what is *tevuna*, what we really understood, like our *meshalim*, was the difference between the Americans and the Greeks: how we ourselves have *bina* and *tevuna* and *chachma*, and how within ourselves a new thing is understood from the same *inyan*.

So what we really understood is not even the *Chabad* of the *kelipos* but the *Chabad* of our *kelipa*, because what we really understood is not even the *inyan* of the soul but of our physical nature. And yes, from our physical nature we can understand how it is in general, from a particular to its general: from how it is in our *bina*, how it is in the general *bina* of the *kelipos*; from that, how it is in the general *bina* of the spiritual worlds of *Beriya, Yetzira and Asiya*; and from there we can try to go up to understand how it is in *Atzilus* and even higher.

Take chapters one, two and three, which were just learned. What we understood there was not the whole *klal* of "His understanding is unsearchable". What we really understood is what our own *tevuna* is. "But we understood that really good. We *mamash* understood that." It is not like the guy who says, "Oh, all is one and one is all," who really did not understand how it works. What we understood, we brought very close to our mind, to where we *mamash* understood it. And not only did we understand it: we understood it in a way that we can now turn around and explain it exactly to somebody else, and even make up new *meshalim* that will fit their kind of brain.

So in a way it is not really like chapters one and two; it almost seems, what are you talking about? It is not really about *Elokus* (G-dliness) at all, it is basically about how the human mind works. That is what "one is not like the other" means: it does not seem you are getting to the goal. "Our goal was, and we're not trying to become psychologists over here, we're trying to understand G-dliness. And instead we're learning psychology. Yeah, we understood it very well, but it's just psychology is what it is."

Fine: but from that, from "from my flesh I see G-d", we can understand a higher *klal*, which then becomes a *prat* of a higher *klal*, which then becomes a *prat* of a higher *klal*, **until he comes to the general comprehension as a whole**: till you can finally understand how it is in the *Chabad* of the *Or Ein Sof*.

What do you mean, you understand the *Chabad* of the *Or Ein Sof*? You have no idea what the *mahus* (what it is in itself) of that is. If you *mamash* knew what it was, you would be able to do the same thing: you would be able to create a world. But it does not matter. We understand the *metzius* (existence) of the relationship between these *inyanim*.

blocks.title: Why you want a steak
blocks.text: As was learned about *Adam Kadmon*: there is no *taanug* (delight) without *ratzon* (will) and no *ratzon* without *taanug*. But we understand it really by us. We say, "Yeah, that's right, that makes sense": when I want something it is because I enjoy it, and I enjoy it because I want it. That is *mamash* how it works; I really understand that. And it is the same on any level, in your own self or on an external, totally material level: you like a steak. Why do you want a steak? Because you enjoy it. And why do you enjoy it? Because you are hungry and you want a steak.

The same way, you see that it works also in a more refined thing, in honor or in *sechel* (intellect). Going up the spiritual ladder from *mamash* a physical steak to *sechel*: why do you enjoy a certain *sechel*, and why do you want it? You see that the *ratzon* and *taanug* are *mamash* one. And from this you can understand the relationship between *ratzon* and *taanug* all the way up to the *ratzon* and *taanug* of the *Atzmus*, which you *mamash* cannot understand, because it is part of the *Atzmus* itself, totally *hiyuli* (formless potential), and *mamash* does not exist. Nonetheless you understand that there is no *ratzon* without *taanug* and no *taanug* without *ratzon*. You *mamash* understand the relationship.

"Where are we?" **And then it is truer, without fooling himself at all.** When he sees it this way, the thing really becomes a true *inyan* by him, without fooling himself and without making mistakes at all, like the mistake talked about earlier.

sections.title: Bottom-up, from the orbits to Elokim: the sweater, the gas bill and the oranges
sections.summary: The particular contemplation runs the other way from the book's explanation: from the *galgalim* and the angels up through each world's *sefiros* to *Malchus* of *Atzilus*, the Name *Elokim*. Followed link by link, from the sweater and the gas bill to the culprit, it makes G-d close and undeniable, the way an engineer, not a passenger, knows an airplane.

phrases.he: כמו כשתחלה יתבונן דרך פרט בממלא כל עלמין
phrases.en: For instance, when first he contemplates in a particular way in *memalei kol almin*:

phrases.he: באיכות התהוות שרש שפע ברוחניות דגלגלים ומזלות
phrases.en: how the root of the flow into the spirituality of the *galgalim* and the *mazalos* comes to be,

phrases.he: מאין ליש דעשיה,
phrases.en: from nothing to something, in *Asiya*,

phrases.he: משמרי האופנים
phrases.en: from the *Shemarei Ofanim* (the dregs of the *Ofanim*).

blocks.text: The example: first he contemplates in a particular way how the spirituality of the *galgalim* (the celestial orbits) and the *mazalos* (the constellations) comes into being from nothing to something in *Asiya*, from the *Shemarei Ofanim* (the *shemarim*, the dregs, of the *Ofanim*, a class of angels). And notice that what he is talking about here is completely backwards from how the book works. "The book is top-down. This is down-up. This is bottom-up."

The book's explanation is top-down, but later, when you think it over, you are supposed to take it from the part that you understand. Not only that: as was said, even when the explanation is from the top down, we understand it down here, how it is down here. And afterwards, once he understands how the actual physical world comes out from the *Shemarei Ofanim*...

phrases.he: ואחר כך יתבונן בפרטיות באופנים וחיות כו'
phrases.en: And afterwards he contemplates in particular the *Ofanim* and the *Chayos*,

phrases.he: עד בחינת מלכות דעשיה,
phrases.en: up to *Malchus* of *Asiya*,

phrases.he: כללות האור האלקי שמהוה עולם העשיה
phrases.en: the whole of the G-dly light that brings the world of *Asiya* into being.

phrases.he: ועל דרך זה בפרטי י׳ ספירות דעשיה
phrases.en: And in this way in the particulars of the ten *sefiros* of *Asiya*,

phrases.he: עד בחינת מלכות דיצירה שנעשה כתר לעשיה
phrases.en: up to *Malchus* of *Yetzira*, which becomes the *Keser* of *Asiya*.

phrases.he: וכן על דרך זה בפרטיות דיצירה
phrases.en: And so too, in this way, in the particulars of *Yetzira*

phrases.he: ובפרטיות דבריאה כו'
phrases.en: and in the particulars of *Beriya*.

blocks.text: **And afterwards he contemplates in particular the *Ofanim* and the *Chayos***: then he will be able to understand something about the angels, and from there the next level up, the chambers of *Malchus* of *Asiya*, **the whole of the G-dly light that brings the world of *Asiya* into being**. (The class stops to check a word: "What do you have there, world?" "No, world": the world of *Asiya*.)

**And in this way in the particulars of the ten *sefiros* of *Asiya***: once you understand how it is in *Malchus* of *Asiya*, you can understand higher and higher, through the *sefiros* of *Asiya* all the way up to *Keser* of *Asiya*. And from *Keser* of *Asiya* you can understand the inner part of *Malchus* of *Yetzira*, **which becomes the *Keser* of *Asiya***.

**And so too, in this way, in the particulars of *Yetzira***: in the same way you can go up the ladder, "like Jacob's ladder", through the levels of *Yetzira*, and then of *Beriya*. And this is also the *inyan* of *tefilla* (prayer): *hisbonenus* is *avoda* (divine service), and *avoda* is *tefilla*. The *inyan* of *tefilla* is to go up the ladder.

phrases.he: עד בחינת מלכות דאצילות
phrases.en: up to *Malchus* of *Atzilus*,

phrases.he: כללות הכל כו'
phrases.en: the whole of everything,

phrases.he: שנקרא שם אלהי״ם בכלל כידוע
phrases.en: which is called, in general, the Name *Elokim*, as is known.

blocks.text: **Up to *Malchus* of *Atzilus***: till you get to *Keser* of *Beriya*, and then you understand how *Malchus* of *Atzilus* becomes *Keser* of *Beriya*. *Malchus* of *Atzilus* is **the whole of everything**, the general thing that includes all the worlds of *Beriya, Yetzira and Asiya*, and that is *yichuda tata'a*.

And he is not talking about the explanation here, because the explanation goes from up to down. He is talking about seeing it: the *inyan* of "Lift up your eyes on high". Once you have the explanation in particular, you can literally look at the world.

blocks.title: I have to wear a sweater because of the galgalim
blocks.text: Take the *galgalim* and *mazalos*. You say: look, it's cold today, that means it's winter. Why is it winter? Because we are in that part of the *mazalos*, with the turnings of the *galgalim*, that makes it winter. That is why all the leaves are falling down, "and that's why I have to wear a sweater." You say: "Wow, look at that. I have to wear a sweater because of the *galgalim*." Now this is something that is *mamash* affecting me.

blocks.title: The gas bill
blocks.text: Not only that: money. "In terms of money, you don't have to worry about it so much, but in terms of money, right now, my heater is on. And the bill is going to hit me at the end of the month." Why is this bill hitting me? "We're talking now about my pocketbook. I could buy stuff with that money." But you see, the *galgalim* and *mazalos* are causing my money to go on gas. My money! We are talking now about a totally physical being, who can see that this is affecting him: I have to have a sweater, I have to walk around with earmuffs, and I have to have my heat on.

blocks.title: From the guy next door to Israel and the Arabs
blocks.text: This is *mamash* my particular life; I am not even talking yet about other people. Then you can look into the *klal* of it too. Since this is affecting me, it must be affecting the guy next door. And since it is affecting the guy next door, it must be affecting all the guys in the whole of Pittsburgh. Not only the whole of Pittsburgh: the whole of northern America. So it can affect the whole price of gas, and so the whole price of energy, and so it could have something to do with the situation with Israel and the Arabs. You go up from level to level with the *pratim*. And what is affecting all of that? The *galgalim*: which of the *mazalos* we are under.

"Okay, where are we now?" **The Name *Elokim***: from this you can go up and up and up, from the *galgalim* to the *Ofanim*, from the *Ofanim* to *Malchus* of *Asiya*, and all the way up to *Malchus* of *Atzilus*, which includes the whole of the external worlds of *Beriya, Yetzira and Asiya*, **which is called, in general, the Name *Elokim***.

phrases.he: שאז מתאמת הדבר יותר בקירוב כו',
phrases.en: For then the thing is truer, closer.

phrases.he: כי אחר העיון היטב בכל הפרטים,
phrases.en: For after a good *iyun* in all the particulars,

phrases.he: הגם שכל פרט בפני עצמו אינו ענין אלהות בכללות
phrases.en: even though each particular by itself is not G-dliness as a whole

phrases.he: ואינו רק בחינת טפל פרטי לבד,
phrases.en: and is only a *tefel*, particular thing,

phrases.he: אבל כאשר יתחבר כל העיון מכל הפרטים אל הכלל,
phrases.en: but when the whole *iyun* of all the particulars is joined to the general,

phrases.he: אז יוקבע יותר בנפש בחינת הכלל
phrases.en: then the general is fixed more in the soul,

phrases.he: כאשר בדוק ומנוסה לכל עוסק בעמקות בהתבוננות
phrases.en: as is tested and tried by everyone who is occupied deeply in contemplation.

blocks.text: **For then the thing is truer, closer**; as he reads it, "then the thing truly comes out close". So I say: really, G-d is affecting the fact that my gas bill is high. Whose fault is that? It's the Name *Elokim*. It's not just a coincidence.

blocks.title: Who got me the orange
blocks.text: Then you can say it about all these things. On *Shabbos* we had some real good food. Where did that come from? From the sun and the moon and the water and the earth. And all of that was affected by certain years: remember the year there was a drought, and another year there was a frost, and the oranges got expensive and you couldn't get oranges. Who did that? Everybody says, "Oh, the *Aibershter* is giving us the oranges." But this means that I am actually following the trail of how exactly the *Aibershter* is giving me oranges.

blocks.title: Columbo finds the culprit
blocks.text: "What do you mean, the *Aibershter*? The *Aibershter* didn't give me the orange, I bought it in the store." Yes, but the *galgalim* affect how much money you have, and the *galgalim* affect how much the oranges are going to cost. And who affects the *galgalim*? The angels. And who affects the angels? *Malchus* of *Asiya*. So you follow the trail up, like a private investigator, like Columbo, and you find out who done it. Who did this to me? Who made it that I don't get my oranges this year, or that this year I do get a lot of oranges and they're very cheap? "Well, you see, the culprit of everything is the *Aibershter*, is *Malchus* of *Atzilus*, *Elokim*."

And then the thing truly comes out close. Then it is not a thing that somebody could come and spin me a tale and convince me that there is no G-d. "What do you mean? I can show you the whole trail, how G-d got me the orange."

**Even though each particular by itself is not G-dliness as a whole**: not only that, it could be totally not an *inyan* of *Elokus*. The first *prat* we started with was that I have to wear a sweater because it is cold outside. What does that have to do with *Elokus* at all? **And is only a *tefel*.** "How do you say *tefel* in English?" "Secondary." Not even secondary: it is not the main thing, a *prat* that you wonder why you would even talk about it. "We want to talk about G-d and you're talking about your sweater and your gas bill."

blocks.title: The airplane engineer
blocks.text: **When the whole *iyun* of all the particulars is joined to the general**: once you put the whole thing together with all the *pratim*, you have an airplane. It is like the guy who knows what an airplane is. I know it's an airplane, you know it's an airplane; who didn't hear of an airplane? Everybody knows what an airplane is. Yes, but the airplane engineer knows every little screw of the airplane and where it goes. He *mamash* knows what the airplane is all about, and he knows all the aerodynamics of it.

blocks.title: Go and make an airplane
blocks.text: I know an airplane can fly, you know an airplane can fly. Why can it fly? "Well, it has wings." Good: so go and make an airplane. Let's see you make a thing with wings; you throw it, and it falls down and doesn't fly. It is not just the wings. The engineer knows exactly how the wings work to make the airplane fly. Here too, it is not just that I know in general, well, there's a G-d in the world and He makes it work, the way the propeller and the wings make the airplane work. You know each little part particularly.

blocks.title: Algebra class, and the ABC before the needle
blocks.text: Even though each part is only a particular. The engineer goes to school, to the screw class and the propeller class and the aerodynamics class, and his algebra class, and he says: what does algebra have to do with anything? "I want to be an airplane guy and you're teaching me algebra." This has nothing to do with anything. Or a little kid goes to school and says, "I want to be a doctor." They say, "Okay. A, B, C, D, E, F, G." "What do you mean? I want to be a doctor. Give me a needle and I'll start sticking people." "No, first you have to learn all the *pratim*, then you'll be able to actually be a doctor."

So even though each thing is only a particular *prat*, **when the whole *iyun* of all the particulars is joined to the general, then the general is fixed more in the soul**. As was said before, the real thing is *davka* the *klal*; but *davka* when you know all the *pratim* do you really know the *klal*. **As is tested and tried**: this has already been tested and tried by anybody who has really done the proper, deepest *hisbonenus*.

sections.title: The higher unity in particulars, and the delusions of the merely general
sections.summary: In *yichuda ila'a* too, knowing how each *partzuf* comes from the one above it, up to the *Kav*, the *tzimtzum* and the infinite light, fixes the Emanator's Essence in the soul; "there's a G-d and finished" sees Him from afar. Whoever squeezes his whole mind onto one vague general idea can fall into false imaginings, while the same depth of *daas* poured into each particular is the opposite of error.

phrases.he: וגם ביחודא עילאה
phrases.en: And so too in *yichuda ila'a*:

phrases.he: בהתבוננות דרך פרט
phrases.en: contemplation in a particular way

phrases.he: בכל פרטי העשר ספירות
phrases.en: in all the particulars of the ten *sefiros*,

phrases.he: בפרצופים דזעיר אנפין ונוקבא ואבא ואמא ואריך אנפין ועתיק יומין
phrases.en: in the *partzufim* of *Zeir Anpin* and *Nukva*, *Abba* and *Ima*, *Arich Anpin* and *Atik Yomin*,

phrases.he: עד ראשית הקו באדם קדמון כו'
phrases.en: up to the beginning of the *Kav* in *Adam Kadmon*:

phrases.he: דרך פרט דוקא,
phrases.en: *davka* in a particular way

phrases.he: הוא המועיל לקבוע בנפש מבחינת כללות עצמות המאציל הכוללם יחד
phrases.en: is what helps to fix in the soul the whole of the Essence of the Emanator, which includes them all together.

blocks.text: **And so too in *yichuda ila'a***: when you know it in a particular way, in all the particulars of the ten *sefiros* and the *partzufim* (the statures of the *sefiros*), *Zeir Anpin* and *Nukva*, *Abba* and *Ima*, *Arich Anpin* and *Atik Yomin*: how they work and how each one connects with the other. It is not just saying, well, *Zeir Anpin*, it's the light of G-d. You know exactly how *Zeir Anpin* and *Nukva* come from *Abba* and *Ima*, and how *Abba* and *Ima* come from *Arich* and *Atik*, up to *Adam Kadmon*, like the *inyan* in chapter 18.

**Davka in a particular way**, knowing everything in particular, **is what helps to fix in the soul the whole of the Essence of the Emanator, which includes them all together**. And that is what you really wanted to know: not even *Malchus* of *Atzilus*.

From *Malchus* of *Atzilus* you go to the unions of *Zeir Anpin* and *Nukva*, from those to the unions of *Abba* and *Ima*, then to how it comes down from *Arich* and *Atik*, and how *Arich* and *Atik* come out from *Adam Kadmon*, all the way to the beginning of the line. And then you can go to how the line comes out after the impression left after the *tzimtzum*, and before that impression there is the *tzimtzum* and the infinite light.

Then it is not just: well, there's an infinite light. And what's the infinite light? "Well, it's, you know, like a light bulb you have, it's a big light bulb." That's basically the way they understand it. And when he knows all the *inyanim* of all the *partzufim*, they say: what's the thing with *partzufim*, with this, with that, what do you have to know all these *partzufim* for? "There's a G-d, and there's a G-d, and finished." You say no: when you know the things **in a particular way**, *davka*, that is what brings the soul to the whole of the Essence of the Emanator, which includes them all together.

phrases.he: מה שאין כן ההתבוננות דרך כלל לבד
phrases.en: Not so contemplation in a general way alone:

phrases.he: כנזכר לעיל שמרחוק יהו״ה נראה לו
phrases.en: as said above, G-d appears to him from afar,

phrases.he: (עד שיוכל ליפול בדמיונות כוזבות כשוטים וחסרי הדעת
phrases.en: (until he can fall into false imaginings, like fools and those who lack *daas*,

phrases.he: מצד צמצום כלי מוחו רק בדבר א'
phrases.en: because he contracts the vessels of his mind into only one thing,

phrases.he: והוא כללי כו')
phrases.en: and that a general one.)

blocks.text: **Not so contemplation in a general way alone**, when the *hisbonenus* is just "well, there's a G-d in the world": **G-d appears to him from afar**. Then he sees G-d from very, very far away.
**Until he can fall into false imaginings, like fools and those who lack *daas***: then he can fall into total *avoda zara* (idolatry) things, "like the idiots and the *chasrei daas*".

sensitivity.reason: Says the merely general meditator can fall into "total avoda zara things, like the idiots", of people who practise such meditation.
sensitivity.publishable: **Until he can fall into false imaginings, like fools and those who lack *daas***.

blocks.text: After the tape is turned: these people, what do they do? "They sit and they meditate on the *omka d'chula*," on the depth of everything, that there is a G-d and He is infinite and stuff like that. And they actually have visions, *mamash*: they have imaginations, false imaginations, "like the total idiots".

sensitivity.reason: Calls people who practise this kind of meditation, and have visions from it, "total idiots".
sensitivity.publishable: After the tape is turned: what do such people do? They sit and meditate on the *omka d'chula*, the depth of everything, that there is a G-d and He is infinite. And they actually have visions, *mamash*: they have imaginations, false imaginations, of the kind the text calls foolish.

blocks.text: Why? **Because he contracts the vessels of his mind into only one thing**: he is concentrating his whole brain into just one thing, **and that a general one**, a general, vague *inyan*.

phrases.he: אבל צמצום העמקת הדעת בכל פרט
phrases.en: But the contraction of *ha'amakas hadaas* (deep concentration) into each particular

phrases.he: הוא ההיפוך מן הטעות
phrases.en: is the opposite of mistake

phrases.he: והריחוק
phrases.en: and of distance.

phrases.he: אדרבא,
phrases.en: On the contrary:

phrases.he: על ידי זה מתקרב הדבר יותר אצלו
phrases.en: through this the thing comes closer to him,

phrases.he: בהיותו הולך מפרט לפרט העליון הימנו עד שכוללם יחד,
phrases.en: as he goes from a particular to the particular above it, until he includes them all together,

phrases.he: ליחד יחוד כללי
phrases.en: to make a *yichud klali* (general unification)

phrases.he: ולא יחוד פרטי
phrases.en: and not a *yichud prati* (particular unification),

phrases.he: כמו לך יהו״ה הגדולה כו'
phrases.en: like "Yours, G-d, is the greatness."

blocks.question: "Wait a minute": chapter 1 said we are supposed to have *amkus hadaas* (depth of *daas*), that it is the *kli* (vessel) for everything. Is this not the same thing?
blocks.text: Yes, but the *kli* is not *amkus hadaas* just to sit and meditate on the final *klal* you are supposed to get to. You have *hisbonenus* in every *prat*, and then *amkus hadaas* in every *prat*: when you are learning this *prat* you are totally concentrated into understanding this *prat* and no other *prat*.

That **is the opposite of mistake and of distance**: of seeing it only in a faraway, vague way, which you really do not understand and can turn upside down. **On the contrary**, just the opposite: **through this the thing comes closer to him**, till he connects all of them in a general unification. Then it is not a thing seen from far away. He connects all the *pratim* and knows the thing with all its *pratim*, like a doctor knows the body, not just in general, or like the engineer knows the airplane.
**Like "Yours, G-d, is the greatness."** Now he is going to explain what a *yichud prati* is and what a *yichud klali* is.

sections.title: Particular unifications, and the one general unification
sections.summary: Following one attribute, like *chesed*, through every world is only a *yichud prati*, and taking one attribute for the whole is a mistake. Each unification is only a detail of a higher one; the *yichud klali* is the *bittul* of the whole chain of the *Kav* to the Essence of the *Or Ein Sof*.

phrases.he: שענין היחוד האלקי הוא בחינת עומק ההשגה
phrases.en: For the G-dly unification is the depth of comprehension,

phrases.he: בביטול היש לאין
phrases.en: in the *bittul* of the *yesh* (something) to the *ayin* (nothing),

phrases.he: ביחודא עילאה ויחודא תתאה
phrases.en: in *yichuda ila'a* and *yichuda tata'a*.

blocks.text: **The G-dly unification is the depth of comprehension.** A *yichud prati* is, for instance, the unification of *gedula* (greatness): how *Malchus* of *Asiya* is connected to *Malchus* of *Yetzira*, *Malchus* of *Yetzira* to *Malchus* of *Beriya*, and so on, all the way up to *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof*. But this is only a *yichud prati*. Beyond that, he even connects all the particular unifications to G-d Himself.

That is **the *bittul* of the *yesh* (something) to the *ayin* (nothing), in *yichuda ila'a* and *yichuda tata'a***: the nullification of the *yesh* of the *pratim* to the total *ayin* of understanding the whole thing together.

phrases.he: ויש יחוד פרטי
phrases.en: And there is a particular unification

phrases.he: בדבר פרטי,
phrases.en: in a particular thing,

phrases.he: כמו לך יהו״ה הגדולה
phrases.en: like "Yours, G-d, is the greatness":

phrases.he: שהוא בחינת חסד שבמלכות דאצילות
phrases.en: which is the *chesed* in *Malchus* of *Atzilus*

phrases.he: בבי''ע דרך פרט בכל עולם כו'
phrases.en: in *Beriya, Yetzira and Asiya*, in a particular way, in each world.

phrases.he: וגם כללותו אינו אלא פרט
phrases.en: And even the whole of it is only a particular,

phrases.he: מדה א' ממדה שבמלכות כו'
phrases.en: one attribute of the attributes in *Malchus*.

blocks.text: **And there is a particular unification in a particular thing**: **"Yours, G-d, is the greatness"** is **the *chesed* in *Malchus* of *Atzilus***. To understand how the *chesed* of *Atzilus* comes into the *chassadim* (kindnesses) of *Beriya, Yetzira and Asiya*, in each particular world, is only a unification of the *chassadim*.

**And even the whole of it is only a particular.** So even when you understand the whole of it, it is only a *prat*, and it is still a mistake: "like, you know, the people who say G-d is love." So you say: if G-d is love, why do so many bad things happen? What happened to justice?

sensitivity.reason: "The people who say G-d is love" points, without naming it, at another religion's creed, as an example of a mistake.
sensitivity.publishable: **And even the whole of it is only a particular.** So even when you understand the whole of it, it is only a *prat*, and taking it for the whole is still a mistake. Say that G-d is only love: then why do so many bad things happen? What happened to justice?

blocks.text: Why? Because they follow one *prat*. They do not even get the *prat*; really they take the whole thing as a *klal*. But if you only know the *inyanim* of the *chassadim*, the right line and not the left line, you cannot put them together to go the next step higher. It is only a *prat* of **one attribute**, the attribute in *Malchus* of *Atzilus*, meaning *chesed* of *Malchus* of *Atzilus*; and the same with *gevura*.

phrases.he: ולך יהו״ה הגבורה
phrases.en: And "Yours, G-d, is the might,"

phrases.he: בכללותו ופרטיו בכל עולם נקרא יחוד פרטי
phrases.en: in its whole and its particulars in each world, is called a *yichud prati*.

phrases.he: ועל דרך זה בכל יחודים פרטיים שבי׳ ספירות דבי''ע כידוע
phrases.en: And so in all the particular unifications of the ten *sefiros* of *Beriya, Yetzira and Asiya*, as is known.

blocks.text: The *gevura*, too, **in its whole and its particulars in each world, is called a *yichud prati***, **and so in all the particular unifications of the ten *sefiros***. So you learn all the *pratim*, and then the unifications of the *pratim*, till you can unify all the *sefiros* in the upper worlds with the same *sefiros* in the lower worlds.

phrases.he: אבל יחוד הכללי הוא כמו מה שכתוב הנה מקום אתי
phrases.en: But the general unification is like what is written, "Behold, there is a place with Me",

phrases.he: או המלך המרומם כו'
phrases.en: or "the exalted King",

phrases.he: המתנשא מכל ימות עולם
phrases.en: "who is raised above all the days of the world":

phrases.he: דו׳ קצוות ומוחין חכמה ובינה שבהם כו'
phrases.en: the six directions, and the *mochin*, *chachma* and *bina*, in them.

phrases.he: וגם זה פרט יחשב
phrases.en: And even this is considered a particular

phrases.he: לגבי עצמות בחינת המלכות שהוא כתר מל'
phrases.en: compared to the Essence of *Malchus*, which is the *Keser* of *Malchus*.

blocks.text: **But the general unification is like what is written, "Behold, there is a place with Me"**: the whole place of the world is by Me. To understand that a world is nothing but G-dliness, and to really understand what that means.
That is, "not according to the *avoda zara* (idolatry) means".

sensitivity.reason: Calls the other understanding of "the world is nothing but G-dliness" (the world itself as G-d, as other religions or pantheism hold) idolatry.

blocks.text: **Or "the exalted King"**: the *Aibershter* is King of the whole world. **"Who is raised above all the days of the world"**, the six directions, and the *mochin*, *chachma* and *bina*, in them ("*chesed* and *bina*... oh sorry, *chachma* and *bina*"): how the actual *Aibershter* is totally higher than the whole ten *sefiros*, and even than the ten essential *sefiros*.

**And even this is considered a particular.** Now he is talking within *Atzilus*: the ten *sefiros* of *Malchus* of *Atzilus*, to understand how the King is totally higher than all its actual separate *sefiros*. And even that is only a *prat* compared to the actual inner part of *Malchus* of *Atzilus*, **which is the *Keser* of *Malchus***.

phrases.he: וכה"ג בע"ס דאצי' כו'
phrases.en: And likewise in the ten *sefiros* of *Atzilus*,

phrases.he: עד עצמות בחינת מלכות דאין סוף בראשית הקו,
phrases.en: up to the Essence of *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof* at the beginning of the *Kav*:

phrases.he: יש יחודים פרטים הרבה בכל ספירה ופרצוף כו'
phrases.en: there are many particular unifications in every one of the *sefiros* and *partzufim*;

phrases.he: ויחוד הכללי בכללות ביטול כל ההשתלשלות דקו כו'
phrases.en: and the general unification is in the general *bittul* of the whole chain of descent of the *Kav*

phrases.he: לגבי עצמות אור אין סוף כידוע.
phrases.en: to the Essence of the *Or Ein Sof*, as is known.

blocks.text: **And likewise in the ten *sefiros* of *Atzilus***: besides *Malchus* of *Atzilus*, you go higher and higher in *Atzilus*, **up to the Essence of *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof* at the beginning of the *Kav***, unifying everything into it. **There are many particular unifications in every one of the *sefiros* and *partzufim***: all kinds of details, and unifications of the details. Each unification is a detail compared to another *klal* higher than it. Even when you make a whole big unification, it is still only a detail compared to the next level up.
And then **the general unification**, finally, after this whole thing, is the *bittul* of the whole chain of descent of the *Kav* **to the Essence of the *Or Ein Sof*, as is known**.

sections.title: The particular needs the general, and the general needs the particular
sections.summary: Whoever starts from the general, however hard he works at it, will not have its truth fixed in him like one who reaches it through the particulars. But particulars never put together are no better: the blind men and the elephant. The *Rishonim* already disagreed about the same thing in prayer.

phrases.he: אך הנה מי שלא העמיק דעתו ביחודים פרטים
phrases.en: But one who has not delved with his mind into particular unifications

phrases.he: ומתחיל מבחינת הכלל,
phrases.en: and starts from the general,

phrases.he: גם שבא לו ביגיעה רבה בהשגות רבות
phrases.en: even if it comes to him with great toil, with many comprehensions

phrases.he: באיכות ענין הביטול בכלל,
phrases.en: of how the *bittul* is, in general,

phrases.he: כמו כשלהבת כו' וכהאי גוונא,
phrases.en: like the flame [and the coal] and the like,

phrases.he: לא יוקבע בנפשו אמיתית ענינו כל כך,
phrases.en: the truth of it will not be fixed in his soul so much

phrases.he: כמו אחר עיון היטב בכל פרטיים,
phrases.en: as after a good *iyun* in all the particulars,

phrases.he: עד שמהם יבוא לבחינת בכלל.
phrases.en: until from them he comes to the general.

blocks.text: **But one who has not delved with his mind into particular unifications and starts from the general** says: everything comes from the infinite light. **Even if it comes to him with great toil, with many comprehensions**: he does not just say everything comes from the infinite light, but thinks of it like a soul in the body and like the flame from a coal, and thinks about it really hard, how exactly this *bittul* is. Still, **the truth of it will not be fixed in his soul so much**: the real way it is will not be entrenched in his soul or his mind, **as after a good *iyun* in all the particulars, until from them he comes to the general**.

phrases.he: והיינו דפרט אצטריך לכלל וכלל אצטריך לפרט,
phrases.en: That is, the particular needs the general and the general needs the particular,

phrases.he: מפני שאין כלל בלא פרט כו'
phrases.en: for there is no general without a particular.

blocks.text: **The particular needs the general and the general needs the particular.** To really do it properly, you cannot just get totally hung up on the *pratim*. The thing with the *pratim* is that you then have to make the unification of the *pratim* into a *klal*. A guy who just knows what the screws are and does not know how they go together will never be able to make an airplane either.

blocks.title: The blind men and the elephant
blocks.text: Like the seven blind men with the elephant: one thought an elephant is like a palm tree, and this one thought an elephant is like a broom. Why? Because they did not realize that each one was holding a *prat*. So going only the way of the *prat* is also not good by itself.

"And this is, by the way, the way of the scientists": they just learned the *pratim* and never tried to put them together into a *klal*. "Says, yeah, okay, I mean, there's a thing." And that is why they think the *pratim* somehow work by themselves.

sensitivity.reason: A sweeping remark about scientists as a group: they only collect details and think the details work by themselves.
sensitivity.publishable: This is the way of anyone who learns the *pratim* and never tries to put them together into a *klal*: in the end he thinks the *pratim* somehow work by themselves.

blocks.text: **For there is no general without a particular**, and no *prat* without a *klal*. To understand a thing properly you have to know all its *pratim*, and when you know all its *pratim*, then you can understand the *klal*.

phrases.he: (ודבר זה כבר נחלקו בו הרבה מגדולי הראשונים כמו הרמב''ם והטור,
phrases.en: (Many of the great *Rishonim* (early authorities) already disagreed about this, like the *Rambam* and the Tur:

phrases.he: אם לכוון בפירוש המלות דרך פרט בגדלות יהו״ה,
phrases.en: whether to have in mind the meaning of the words in a particular way, the greatness of G-d,

phrases.he: אם לכוון דרך כלל,
phrases.en: or to have in mind in a general way

phrases.he: לפני מי אתה עומד ומתפלל כו'
phrases.en: "before Whom you stand and pray",

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב בכתבים)
phrases.en: as is written in the writings.)

blocks.question: In prayer, what are you really supposed to think of: the particular meaning of each word, or only "before Whom you stand"?
blocks.text: Here he is talking about the *avoda* of *tefilla*, which is the whole *inyan* of *hisbonenus* and going up. **Many of the great *Rishonim* (early authorities) already disagreed about this, like the *Rambam* and the Tur.** When you say "Yours, G-d, is the greatness", are you supposed to think of *gedula*, and when you say "the might", think of *gevura*, and so on in all the *kavanos* (intentions)? Or should you just think: I am standing in front of the *Aibershter*?

sections.title: Every particular aimed at the Essence
sections.summary: A general and a particular thought cannot be held at once, but whoever wants only the Essence directs every particular to it, more truly than one who thinks of the Essence directly. The particulars, even when they look like psychology, are studied only to reach Him, never as a subject for itself, and so too the *Zohar* and the *Arizal*, as the Alter Rebbe heard from the *Maggid*.

phrases.he: והגם שהמחשבה כללית עם המחשבה פרטית לא ישכנו כאחד,
phrases.en: And although a general thought and a particular thought cannot dwell together,

phrases.he: מכל מקום מי שהוא מעמיק בכל לבו ובכל חפצו
phrases.en: nevertheless, one who is *ma'amik* (delving) with all his heart and all his desire

phrases.he: לעצמות האלקות דוקא,
phrases.en: *davka* to the Essence of G-dliness:

phrases.he: הנה גם בעיונו בפרטיות יכוין הכל אל המחשבה הכללית דעצמות דוקא
phrases.en: even in his *iyun* in the particulars he will direct it all to the general thought of the Essence, *davka*.

blocks.text: **A general thought and a particular thought cannot dwell together**: you cannot think about two things at once. If you are thinking about before Whom you are standing, then you are thinking about before Whom you are standing. If you are thinking of *Malchus* of *tevuna*, then you are thinking of that.

**Nevertheless, one who is *ma'amik* (delving) with all his heart and all his desire *davka* to the Essence of G-dliness.** Right now it seems we are learning one *prat*, then another *prat*: now only about *bina*, now about *chachma*. But since we are *ma'amik* with all the heart and desire to the *Atzmus* of *Elokus*, *davka*, **even in his *iyun* in the particulars he will direct it all to the general thought of the Essence**. Even when it seems we are talking about human psychology, we know that that is not at all what we are talking about: the *kavana* (intention) is *mamash* to the *Atzmus*. Not only that: the *machshava* (thought) is more to the *Atzmus* than that of somebody whose intention is on the *Atzmus* itself.

phrases.he: ולא יפול מכללות הכונה כלל
phrases.en: And he will not fall at all from the whole of the *kavana*

phrases.he: מחמת צמצום הכונה הפרטיות,
phrases.en: because of the contraction of the particular *kavana*,

phrases.he: מאחר שכל הפרטים אינם נמשכים והולכים רק אחר הכלל דוקא,
phrases.en: since all the particulars are drawn and go only after the general, *davka*,

phrases.he: כידוע לכל הולך בדרך אמת,
phrases.en: as is known to everyone who goes in the way of truth,

phrases.he: ליהו״ה לבדו דוקא,
phrases.en: to G-d alone, *davka*;

phrases.he: כמו שכתבו זכרונם לברכה אליו ולא למדותיו
phrases.en: as our Sages, of blessed memory, wrote: "to Him, and not to His attributes."

blocks.text: **And he will not fall at all from the whole of the *kavana*.** It will not at all disturb the *kavana* to the *etzem* of the *Aibershter* Himself that you are just talking about little particular details, which, as was said, are really not even about *tevuna* or *bina* or *chachma* or *Malchus* of *Atzilus*: we are really talking about our particular *kelipa*. It makes no difference. Since our intention is truly to the *Aibershter*, not only does it not disturb, just the opposite: it is what makes the *kavana* proper.

**Since all the particulars are drawn and go only after the general, *davka***: all the *pratim* he is talking about and thinking about go only after the *klal* of the *Aibershter* Himself, as is known to anybody who learns the proper way, *davka* to the *Aibershter*, and as the Sages said: **"to Him, and not to His attributes."** Our whole *kavana* in this whole study is *davka* to the *Aibershter* Himself, and has nothing to do with the *middos* at all.

phrases.he: רק כללות ענין ההתבוננות בפרטי מדותיו
phrases.en: Only, the whole matter of contemplating the particulars of His attributes

phrases.he: הוא רק כדי שיבא לעצמותו ומהותו דוקא
phrases.en: is only so that he come to His Essence and His *mahus*, *davka*;

phrases.he: ולא לכוון העיקר רק בכוונה של הפרט,
phrases.en: and not to make the main intention the *kavana* of the particular,

phrases.he: כמו בשביל איזה לימוד לעצמו.
phrases.en: as for some study for itself.

blocks.text: **The whole matter of contemplating the particulars of His attributes is only so that he come to His Essence and His *mahus***: that is the main thing our intention is on. **And not to make the main intention the *kavana* of the particular, as for some study for itself**, like a person who wants to learn something for himself.

Like an etymologist or a psychologist: he wants to learn what *bina* is and what *chachma* is, and what he is really learning is the *inyan* of *bina* and *chachma*. What we are learning has nothing to do with *bina* and *chachma* at all. We are learning about the *Aibershter*.

phrases.he: גם בעיונו בספר הזוהר ובכתבי האריז''ל
phrases.en: Also in his *iyun* in the *Zohar* and in the writings of the *Arizal*,

phrases.he: צריך להיות על דרך זה דוקא
phrases.en: it must be *davka* in this way;

phrases.he: ודי למבין
phrases.en: and this is enough for one who understands.

phrases.he: (וכאשר מקובל היה אבי אדוני מורי ורבי זכרונו לברכה נשמתו עדן בדבר זה
phrases.en: (As my father, my master, my teacher and my Rebbe, of blessed memory, whose soul is in Eden, received on this matter

phrases.he: מפי הרב המגיד זכרונו לברכה בפירוש גמור
phrases.en: from the mouth of the Rav, the *Maggid*, of blessed memory, explicitly;

phrases.he: וכך שמעתי מפיו זכרונו לברכה)
phrases.en: and so I heard from his mouth, of blessed memory.)

blocks.text: **Also in his *iyun* in the *Zohar* and in the writings of the *Arizal***: "like some people want to look in the *Zohar* to find out about demons or something like that, you know. That's what they want to find out." **It must be *davka* in this way**, all of it. **And this is enough for one who understands.**

**As my father... received on this matter from the mouth of the Rav, the *Maggid***: "my father" means the Alter Rebbe. The *Mitteler Rebbe* is saying: I heard from my father that he learned this from the *Maggid*, as an explicit explanation.

sections.title: Kabbalistic meanings do not confuse the general; the beginner; lechatchila ariber
sections.summary: The particular, Kabbalistic meanings do not confuse the general thought; they strengthen it, whatever the complaints against "our way". A beginner davens before the *Aibershter* in general and grows into the particulars. And for us, after the Rebbe's two *lechatchila aribers*, this is not a tract on contemplation but *Shaar HaYichud*, the beginning of the work of *Moshiach*: to know G-d.

phrases.he: ובזה מתורץ שאלת השואלים על פירוש המלות דרך פרט
phrases.en: And with this is answered the question of those who ask about the meaning of the words in a particular way,

phrases.he: ליודעים בהם,
phrases.en: for those who know them:

phrases.he: איך שאינם מבלבלים את מחשבת הכלל
phrases.en: how do they not confuse the general thought?

phrases.he: אלא אדרבא
phrases.en: Rather, on the contrary:

phrases.he: כוונות פירוש המלות על פי המלות עפ"י הקבלה
phrases.en: the *kavanos* of the meaning of the words according to the Kabbalah

phrases.he: מסייעים לחזק את עומק השגת הכלל בעצמות אלקות,
phrases.en: help to strengthen the depth of the comprehension of the general, in the Essence of G-dliness,

phrases.he: כידוע לטועמי טעם בהם דרך פרט כו'
phrases.en: as is known to those who have tasted their taste in a particular way.

blocks.text: **With this is answered the question of those who ask about the meaning of the words in a particular way, for those who know them: how do they not confuse the general thought?** We are still not really *davenen* with the meanings of the words. But about the way we are studying, a lot of people think: what are you studying? The main thing is *ein od milvado* (there is nothing besides Him). You are just *maskilim* (people of intellect), interested in all kinds of Kabbalistic matters. People think you want just *razi li* (my secret is mine), to know all kinds of particular things.

No, it is not like that. And this is a thing the *Mitteler Rebbe* is telling us that his father told him that the *Maggid* told him. It answers what they ask: it does not make a confusion in the understanding of G-dliness. **Rather, on the contrary**, the meaning of the words according to the Kabbalah helps **to strengthen the depth of the comprehension of the general, in the Essence of G-dliness**.

The fact that we are learning all these particular Kabbalistic matters: "Yeah, what do you need to learn Kabbalistic matters? The main thing is there's a G-d, *ein od milvado*." "This is one of the big complaints against our way, you know." **As is known to those who have tasted their taste in a particular way**: to anybody who has really tasted the taste of this learning.

phrases.he: רק החדשים
phrases.en: Only, the new ones:

phrases.he: יותר טוב להם להעמיק דרך כלל תחלה,
phrases.en: it is better for them to delve in a general way first,

phrases.he: עד שיורגלו מעט מעט בדרך הפרט דווקא
phrases.en: until they get used, little by little, to the particular way, *davka*;

phrases.he: ודי למבין:
phrases.en: and this is enough for one who understands.

blocks.question: So what about the *davenen* (praying)? How should we *daven*: should we start *davenen* according to the *kavanos* of the *Arizal*?
blocks.text: He says no. **The new ones**, the people new to this, **it is better for them to delve in a general way first, until they get used, little by little, to the particular way**. When you are *davenen*, just *daven* as if you are in front of the *Aibershter*, until you learn a little better; then you will be able to *daven* like this even in the *davenen*. **And this is enough for one who understands.**

blocks.title: Lechatchila ariber: like Rashbi, who did not have to daven
blocks.text: One of the things to mention here is *lechatchila ariber* (going over the top from the start). The Rebbe said that by us we can go *lechatchila ariber*, and he really meant *lechatchila ariber*, *lechatchila ariber*: even what the Rebbe said was on top of the *lechatchila ariber* the *Rebbe Maharash* said. Meaning that we are going directly, straight, like the Rebbe said, to live like *Moshiach*, "and we don't even have to worry about *davenen*": we can already be like Rashbi, who did not have to *daven*. ("Are you guys still there?" "Yeah, yeah.")

sensitivity.reason: "We don't even have to worry about davenen", taken out of the class, reads as license not to pray; he means that the learning itself is already directed to the Essence.
sensitivity.publishable: One of the things to mention here is *lechatchila ariber* (going over the top from the start). The Rebbe said that by us we can go *lechatchila ariber*, and he really meant *lechatchila ariber*, *lechatchila ariber*: even what the Rebbe said was on top of the *lechatchila ariber* the *Rebbe Maharash* said. Meaning that we are going directly, straight, like the Rebbe said, to live like *Moshiach*: the learning itself, like Rashbi's, is already directed straight to the Essence.

blocks.title: Choni HaMe'agel davened; Rashbi said Chassidus
blocks.text: That Rashbi, they just learned, they did not have to *daven*: like the story of Choni HaMe'agel and Rashbi. Choni HaMe'agel *davened* and he got the rain; Rashbi just said *Chassidus*, and the rain came. So by us, really, we can go totally beyond the whole thing, and not even think of the *Chassidus* as something we have to bring into the *davenen* at all. We can just go *lechatchila ariber*, straight to *daas Havaya* (knowing G-d), and right now, even without *davenen*, our intention is directly to the *Atzmus* in the learning. The whole thing is one.

sensitivity.reason: Continues the point that "even without davenen" the learning suffices; a reader could take it as a rule about prayer.
sensitivity.publishable: That Rashbi just learned: like the story of Choni HaMe'agel and Rashbi. Choni HaMe'agel *davened* and he got the rain; Rashbi just said *Chassidus*, and the rain came. So by us, really, we can go *lechatchila ariber*, straight to *daas Havaya* (knowing G-d): right now, in the learning itself, we are *mechaven* directly to the *Atzmus*. The whole thing is one.

blocks.text: Because these are already the days of *Moshiach*. What he is talking about here in the *davenen* means that first there is the learning and then there is the *davenen*: first the learning of the *inyanim* and the *pratim*, and then the *amkus hadaas* into them, to bring the *kavana*, to be the *kavana* to the *Atzmus* in the *davenen*. That is *avodas halev* (the service of the heart). And the Rebbe said already: we are *lechatchila ariber*.

blocks.title: Two lechatchila aribers: depth within depth
blocks.text: Really, the Rebbe said that when the *Rebbe Maharash* said *lechatchila ariber*, that meant *avodas hamochin* (the service of the mind). And the Rebbe said a second *lechatchila ariber* even on that, which means *omek lifnim m'omek* (a depth within depth): the second depth is not just the same as the first, just a second one; in relation to the first depth, it is depth.

blocks.title: The guy polishing his car
blocks.text: The Rebbe said already that we are in the days of *Moshiach*, and explained what the *Rambam* says: in those days the occupation of the whole world will be only to know G-d, and the whole world will be full of the knowledge of G-d as the waters cover the sea. Everything: even some guy polishing his car in the corner. That seems not just a *prat* that has nothing to do with the *klal*; it seems a *prat* that is opposite to the *klal*. "A *kelipa*. A bad *kelipa*." Even that is *mamash ein od milvado*: even this guy polishing his car is nothing but the *Aibershter* Himself, and we understand it in the proper manner. Not from far away, thinking that the world is G-d or something like that, "which is a really pantheistic nonsense".

We are very lucky to have this, and not only that the Rebbe gave it to us the way the *Mitteler Rebbe* gave it over. A lot of people say, "Oh, you're *chassidim* of the *Mitteler Rebbe*." "It's not true. We are *chassidim* of the Rebbe." Compared to the *chassidim* of the *Mitteler Rebbe*, "we're like, I wouldn't even say babies, we're like amoebas, you know?" As they say: if they were angels, we are people; if they are people, we are donkeys. And yet by them they did not get it the way we do.

sensitivity.reason: Answers people who call us "chassidim of the Mitteler Rebbe" ("It's not true"), and says the Mitteler Rebbe's chassidim "did not get it the way we do": a claim about other approaches within Chabad.
sensitivity.publishable: We are very lucky to have this, and not only that the Rebbe gave it to us the way the *Mitteler Rebbe* gave it over: we are *chassidim* of the Rebbe. Compared to the *chassidim* of the *Mitteler Rebbe*, "we're like, I wouldn't even say babies, we're like amoebas, you know?" As they say: if they were angels, we are people; if they are people, we are donkeys.

blocks.text: Why do we get it in a way they did not? Because we are students of the Rebbe, and we have it with two *lechatchila aribers* on it: first the *Rebbe Maharash* made a *lechatchila ariber*, and then the Rebbe made a *lechatchila ariber* on his *lechatchila ariber*.

So by us this is not a tract of *hisbonenus* anymore. It is *Shaar HaYichud*. They used to call it *Kuntres HaHisbonenus*; by us it is called *Shaar HaYichud*, and if you want to call it a tract, "we should call it" the tract of *daas Havaya*, of knowing G-d. Because by us the *avoda* of *Moshiach* has already started, of which it says that in those days the occupation of the whole world will be only to know G-d. "That's all we're interested in over here. And that's the end of the chapter," and this is enough for one who understands.

reviewQuestions.question: What is the advantage of the general way, and why does the chapter call it the real goal?
How can one who says "all is one and one is all" understand G-dliness the opposite of how it is, and why does the particular way not fall into this?
Why does the particular contemplation go bottom-up, and how does the trail from a sweater or a gas bill lead to the Name *Elokim*?
Why is following *chesed* through all the worlds still only a *yichud prati*, and what is the *yichud klali*?
What do the airplane engineer and the blind men with the elephant each show about the particular and the general?
If a general and a particular thought cannot be held together, how can study of the particulars be directed to the Essence, and how should a beginner *daven*?
